chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdillah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If a fasting man deliberately immerses himself in water, is he required to make up that day?' He said: 'He is not required to make it up, nor does he need to repeat it.'

As for the ruling of the junubi (one in major ritual impurity) at night, the Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) has mentioned that whoever becomes junubi and sleeps with the intention of performing ghusl before dawn, and sleep continues until the sun rises, he is not required to make up the day nor does he pay expiation; rather, he performs ghusl and fasts.
If he wakes up, then sleeps a second time with the intention of performing ghusl before dawn, and sleep continues until sunrise, he is required to make up the day but not pay expiation.
If he sleeps a third time, he is required to make up the day and pay expiation.
As for that which indicates the first case, it is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a fasting person becomes junubi at night and sleeps until dawn?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of the *junubi* who sleeps until dawn, distinguishing between mere omission of ghusl (requiring only *qada*) and deliberate delay with repeated sleep (requiring *kaffarah*). It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on intention (*niyyah*) and the continuity of sleep as factors determining the severity of the ruling, reflecting the nuanced legal methodology of Shaykh al-Tusi.
